vignettes.context: An AI-assisted credit screening system prioritises loan applications for manual review. Human analysts make the final lending decision.
evidence: Validation accuracy: 91.8%.
False-positive rate for demographic group A: 8.1%.
False-positive rate for demographic group B: 8.7%.
False-negative rate for demographic group A: 6.4%.
False-negative rate for demographic group B: 6.8%.
Calibration error: 0.031 for demographic group A and 0.034 for demographic group B.
The validation dataset contains 48,200 applications.
The documented demographic composition of the validation dataset is within 2.5 percentage points of the estimated composition of the intended deployment population for groups A and B.
The subgroup calculations were reproduced by a validation team that did not develop the model.
vignettes.request: Assess whether the available evidence supports attributing fairness to the system for the described deployment context.

vignettes.context: An AI-assisted credit screening system prioritises loan applications for manual review. Human analysts make the final lending decision.
evidence: Validation accuracy: 93.1%.
Overall false-positive rate: 7.9%.
Overall false-negative rate: 6.2%.
Overall calibration error: 0.029.
The validation dataset contains 51,600 applications.
Group-specific error rates are not reported in the validation documentation.
The demographic composition of the validation dataset is not included in the documentation available to the evaluator.
During the first eight weeks of limited deployment, 14,310 applications were processed.
Seven complaints concerning lending decisions were registered; none had completed investigation at the date of evaluation.
vignettes.request: Assess whether the available evidence supports attributing fairness to the system for the described deployment context.

vignettes.context: An AI system classifies medical documents into administrative workflow categories. Staff review classifications before downstream processing.
evidence: Standard validation accuracy: 96.4%.
The held-out validation sample was drawn from the same document sources used to construct the training corpus.
Pilot deployment accuracy: 94.9%.
During the pilot, 18,420 documents were processed.
Human operators modified 3.1% of model classifications before downstream processing.
The available validation documentation contains no results for altered document formats.
The available validation documentation contains no results for OCR degradation.
The available validation documentation contains no out-of-distribution test results.
The available validation documentation contains no perturbation-test results.
vignettes.request: Assess whether the available evidence supports attributing operational robustness to the system for the described deployment context.

vignettes.context: An AI system recommends whether insurance claims should receive additional fraud review. Human reviewers determine the final disposition of individual claims.
evidence: Each model recommendation contains a timestamp and model version.
Human reviewers can accept or override model recommendations.
Overrides are recorded.
Recording a rationale for an override is optional.
The process documentation lists the Fraud Operations team and Automated Decision-Support team as jointly responsible for operation of the process.
The documentation available to the evaluator contains no rule assigning responsibility for an individual decision when the reviewer and model recommendation agree.
Reviewers report that unusual cases are commonly discussed with senior colleagues.
Customers can submit complaints through the organisation's general complaints process.
The process documentation available to the evaluator does not describe how such complaints are connected to reconsideration of the original assessment.
vignettes.request: Assess whether the available evidence supports attributing accountable decision-making to the described AI-assisted process.

vignettes.context: An AI system classifies medical documents into administrative workflow categories. Staff review classifications before downstream processing.
evidence: Standard-condition validation accuracy: 95.2%.
With 10% randomly removed non-critical fields, accuracy was 93.7%.
With the predefined OCR degradation transformation, accuracy was 92.1%.
Across the predefined formatting-variation set, accuracy ranged from 91.6% to 94.8%.
An out-of-distribution test set contained 1,200 documents from document classes excluded from training.
Of the 1,200 out-of-distribution samples, 1,127 were flagged by the out-of-distribution mechanism.
The validation protocol contains three predefined perturbation tests; corresponding accuracies were 92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%.
A separate validation team reproduced the reported tests.
vignettes.request: Assess whether the available evidence supports attributing operational robustness to the system for the described deployment context.

vignettes.context: An AI system recommends whether insurance claims should receive additional fraud review. Human reviewers determine the final disposition of individual claims.
evidence: Each model recommendation record contains the model version, timestamp, and a reference to the input record.
The human review record identifies the evidence consulted.
The final disposition is stored separately from the model recommendation.
Reviewers enter a free-text rationale when finalising a disposition.
The documented procedure assigns the final case-level decision to the claims reviewer.
Disagreements between the model recommendation and the reviewer are routed to an organisational role identified as Senior Claims Reviewer.
Customers may request reconsideration of an adverse disposition.
Reconsideration outcomes are retained with the original decision record.
Model maintenance is assigned to the Model Operations team.
vignettes.request: Assess whether the available evidence supports attributing accountable decision-making to the described AI-assisted process.
